quotes.text: This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Stripe cancels the PaymentIntent and sends a [payment_intent.canceled](https://docs.stripe.com/api/events/types.md#event_types-payment_intent.canceled) event if the payment isn’t captured during the 7-day window.
You can create Mondu payments in the currencies that map to your country. The default local currency for Mondu is `eur`.

findings: The semantic raw delta is navigation only. New raw lines 1–17 capture the November 7, 2026 canonical page title and four variant links, corresponding to old raw lines 8–10, 87–89, 570–572 and 1160–1162. Content diff lines 1–17 and 1392–1397 show replacement of the combined variant body with the selector, without establishing what the linked bodies currently say.

Current source lines 13–21 preserve the four labels, the `mondu` enum and selected PaymentIntent errors, but compress route prerequisites, destination fields and the optional authorization/capture state machine into unscoped claims. Stripe index line 342 and BNPL concept lines 192 and 263 repeat the unscoped route language.

Old raw lines 12–49 and 53–69 describe redirect-based, single-use 30-day net terms and a hosted-style Checkout example with EUR, same-currency line items, `mode: payment` and `success_url`. Old raw lines 95–112 and 125–194 give the same EUR, payment-mode and line-item conditions for Elements with Checkout Sessions, where the server creates the Session and passes its client secret, with `ui_mode: elements` and `return_url`. Checkout support for setup or subscription mode is excluded in both sets of compatibility prose.

Old raw lines 799–933 and 960–981 keep server-created PaymentIntent and client `stripe.confirmPayment` separate, with Customer Accounts v2 `customer_account` and Customers v1 `customer` as separate examples. Old raw lines 1179–1195 and 1268–1362 describe the Direct API PaymentIntent, Stripe.js confirmation and an optional server-driven `requires_action` / `next_action.redirect_to_url` path. Redirect return still calls for status verification, and `payment_intent.succeeded` is the completion signal the old guide recommends for fulfillment workflows.

Paired old capture explicitly dated May 6, 2026 at line 2. Related Mondu overview sections independently preserve general EUR/CHF/GBP by country and standard payout timing, and record May `Connect support: No` versus November `Yes`. Reviewed only the portions recorded above. That dated overview change is separate from the acceptance index, and neither establishes particular Connect routes or account entitlement.
historical_claims_to_preserve: May 6, 2026 full guide remains detailed provenance for Checkout routes, alongside November 7, 2026 navigation provenance. Checkout and Elements Checkout Sessions compatibility prose documents EUR presentment, same-currency line items and payment mode only (old raw lines 18–35, 95–112). Hosted-style Checkout uses `success_url` in the shown example (lines 53–69); Checkout Sessions with Elements passes `return_url` on server-side session creation and gives the Session client secret to the client (lines 125–194).

Distinguish the old Checkout Sessions `initCheckoutElementsSdk`/Checkout session `confirm` integration and its Dahlia script/package minimums as documented on May 6 (old raw lines 204–251, 488–527) from the Elements PaymentIntents client `stripe.confirmPayment` flow and from Direct API optional server redirect (lines 799–981, 1268–1362).

Old raw lines 1094–1140 describe optional PaymentIntent `capture_method: manual`, authorization success leading to `requires_capture`, capture of the entire authorized amount by default or a supplied amount up to it, and automatic cancellation plus `payment_intent.canceled` if uncaptured after seven days. Successful redirect or authorization does not establish capture, payment completion, fulfillment, settlement or funds availability.

Direct API currency-by-country scope with EUR default, CHF for CH and GBP for GB (old raw lines 1376–1380), sandbox-only approve/decline test controls versus live Mondu redirect where described (lines 564–568, 1142–1146), and the PaymentIntent-specific error tables (lines 1148–1158, 1382–1392) remain dated.
conflicts: Baseline route overgeneralization: source lines 17–19, Stripe index line 342, and BNPL concept lines 192 and 263 imply shared `return_url` and capture rules. Preserve route-aware language in reciprocal entries: shown hosted-style Checkout uses `success_url` (old lines 53–69); Elements with Checkout Sessions sets `return_url` on the Session (lines 140–156 and 176–194); Elements with PaymentIntents and Direct API supply `return_url` at confirmation (lines 927–981, 1287–1339); seven-day manual capture belongs to the documented optional PaymentIntent flow (lines 1094–1140).

Old raw line 58 contains a malformed Checkout code comment listing EUR/CHF/GBP and swallowing an apparent currency assignment. The formal Checkout and Checkout Sessions compatibility prose says EUR (old lines 18–35 and 95–112). The broader Mondu overview and old Direct API country map are method-/route-specific, not authority to broaden historical Checkout compatibility.

Separate dated overview conflict: related raw/stripe-mondu-2025.md lines 36–38 says Connect No and raw/stripe-payments-mondu-2026-11-07.md lines 37–39 says Yes. BNPL concept lines 34 and 182 and the linked method overview should preserve date and scope when reconciled by that job. The acceptance index adds no Connect route or entitlement evidence.
unresolved_questions: November linked variant bodies were not supplied or read. Current variant-level API or SDK details, Checkout-specific currency support, merchant/account eligibility and successful runtime behavior remain unverified.

findings: Source line 13 lists the four variants but does not distinguish hosted-style Checkout from Checkout Sessions-backed Elements or date the authority when adding the November selector. Scope lines 17–21 to the historical routes and preserve older raw provenance (lines 6–7 and 23–25).
Make the redirect result/check and optional manual authorization expiry discoverable at the summary level (old raw lines 1076–1140 and 1315–1362).
conflicts: Source line 17 gives blanket `return_url` despite old raw line 68 showing `success_url` for hosted-style Checkout. Line 19 gives seven days without its optional PaymentIntent scope or cancellation consequence. Lines 13 and 19 use Billie/Kriya analogies that do not prove validation or capture equivalence.
source_assessments.reason: A reader asking which field to set for hosted Checkout or when a Mondu PaymentIntent can be captured could select an incorrect field or conflate pending authorization with a completed payment. The current summary directs readers with a blanket answer and does not give a targeted route or state locator. The November index alone is navigational, so the baseline correction should cite the May full guide and the November selector separately.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mondu/accept-a-payment, the November 7, 2026 capture (new raw lines 1-17) establishes navigation to Checkout, Elements with Checkout Sessions API, Elements with Payment Intents API, and Direct API. Their prerequisites and states come from the May 6, 2026 capture. Old raw lines 12-69 document single-use, 30-day net terms and customer authorization by redirect. In old raw lines 18-69 and old raw lines 95-194, the two Checkout routes document EUR, same-currency line items and payment mode only: the hosted-style example uses `success_url`, while Elements with Checkout Sessions uses server-created `ui_mode: elements`, `return_url` and a Session client secret. In old raw lines 799-933 and old raw lines 1179-1362, PaymentIntent routes create the Intent on the server and use Stripe.js confirmation in the client, or optionally handle `requires_action` and `next_action.redirect_to_url` in the Direct API flow. The browser return calls for status verification and does not establish completion. Old raw lines 1076-1140 distinguish `payment_intent.succeeded` from optional manual authorization (`requires_capture`), which expires with cancellation if uncaptured within seven days. `source-stripe-mondu-accept-payment.md` lines 13-21 identify four routes and selected errors but need route-specific return handling and optional capture-state qualifications.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mondu/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 5-17 show a presentation and navigation change from the May 6, 2026 combined guide to a November 7, 2026 selector. No new substantive API or payment behavior is established by the selector. Keep the May 6 guide dated for hosted-style `success_url`, Checkout Sessions with Elements `return_url`, EUR and payment-mode compatibility (old raw lines 18-69 and old raw lines 95-194), and for the separate Direct API EUR-default country map including CHF for CH and GBP for GB (old raw lines 1376-1380). In `source-stripe-mondu-accept-payment.md` lines 13-21 and the reciprocal Stripe BNPL and index routes, scope the return destination to its integration and the seven-day cancellation window to optional manual PaymentIntent capture (old raw lines 1094-1140). Do not generalize the malformed Checkout example comment into a new currency rule. Keep the Checkout-specific client SDK and PaymentIntent confirmation and identity alternatives distinct (old raw lines 204-251 and old raw lines 799-933), as well as sandbox test controls, redirect/action, successful authorization and actual payment completion (old raw lines 1076-1146 and old raw lines 1287-1362). The separate Mondu overview documents a dated May No versus November Yes on Connect (overview raw lines 36-38 and 37-39 respectively); resolve the cross-reference by date and source scope, with no acceptance-flow or account-entitlement inference.
